Every command, as `crossrepo --help` reports it. The python API mirrors it, one
call per command, and is documented in the [API reference](../api/index.qmd).

A `--config PATH` given before a command names the configuration file to use
instead of the one that would be found; `--refresh` before or after one rescans
the repositories rather than reading the stored catalog.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Where settings come from"}
A `crossrepo.toml` in the working directory is read *instead of*
`~/.config/crossrepo/config.toml`, not on top of it, and only the working
directory itself is looked in. `crossrepo config` says which of the two is in
force.
:::

## `crossrepo` {#crossrepo}

```console
crossrepo [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

Catalog and fetch versioned result files across git repos.

| Option | |
|---|---|
| `--config PATH` | path to config.toml |
| `--refresh` | rescan repos instead of using the cached catalog |
| `-V, --version` | Show the version and exit. |

| Subcommand | |
|---|---|
| [`crossrepo cache`](#crossrepo-cache) | Show what the local cache holds, and check that it is sound. |
| [`crossrepo config`](#crossrepo-config) | Show the settings in force, or work on one of the two config files. |
| [`crossrepo get`](#crossrepo-get) | Fetch \[owner/\]repo:path\[@version\] into the cache and print its path. |
| [`crossrepo info`](#crossrepo-info) | Print everything the catalog holds about \[owner/\]repo:path\[@version\]. |
| [`crossrepo list`](#crossrepo-list) | List result files, optionally limited to one repo. |
| [`crossrepo refresh`](#crossrepo-refresh) | Rescan the repos and store the catalog. |
| [`crossrepo repos`](#crossrepo-repos) | Print one line per repo holding result files. |
| [`crossrepo share`](#crossrepo-share) | Publish PATH, saying in DESCRIPTION what it holds. |
| [`crossrepo stamp`](#crossrepo-stamp) | Record what the published symbolic links in a repository point at. |
| [`crossrepo versions`](#crossrepo-versions) | Print the history of one result file, given as \[owner/\]repo:path. |

### `crossrepo cache` {#crossrepo-cache}

```console
crossrepo cache [OPTIONS]
```

Show what the local cache holds, and check that it is sound.

Verification re-hashes every object and compares the digest with the key it
is stored under, so it says whether the cache still holds what it claims.
``--repair`` removes the objects that fail, together with the readable links
that stand for them; their content is fetched again the next time it is
asked for.

| Option | |
|---|---|
| `--verify` | re-hash every cached object and report any that do not match its key |
| `--repair` | remove the objects that fail verification; implies --verify |

### `crossrepo config` {#crossrepo-config}

```console
crossrepo config [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

Show the settings in force, or work on one of the two config files.

Called on its own it shows what is in force and which file that came from:
the crossrepo.toml in this directory when there is one, else the config
that applies everywhere. `config local` and `config global` name one of the
two outright, and write the file if it is not there yet.

A ``--config PATH`` given before the subcommand names the file to show,
instead of the one that would be found.

| Subcommand | |
|---|---|
| [`crossrepo config global`](#crossrepo-config-global) | Write or change the config file that applies everywhere. |
| [`crossrepo config local`](#crossrepo-config-local) | Write or change the crossrepo.toml in this directory. |

#### `crossrepo config global` {#crossrepo-config-global}

```console
crossrepo config global [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

Write or change the config file that applies everywhere.

| Subcommand | |
|---|---|
| [`crossrepo config global append`](#crossrepo-config-global-append) | Add VALUES to the list setting KEY in the config file that applies everywhere. |
| [`crossrepo config global init`](#crossrepo-config-global-init) | Write the config file that applies everywhere, unless it is already there. |
| [`crossrepo config global reset`](#crossrepo-config-global-reset) | Take KEY out of the config file that applies everywhere, so its default applies. |
| [`crossrepo config global set`](#crossrepo-config-global-set) | Set KEY to VALUES in the config file that applies everywhere. |
| [`crossrepo config global show`](#crossrepo-config-global-show) | Print the config file that applies everywhere. |

##### `crossrepo config global append` {#crossrepo-config-global-append}

```console
crossrepo config global append [OPTIONS] KEY VALUES...
```

Add VALUES to the list setting KEY in the config file that applies everywhere.

Takes `KEY` and `VALUES...`.

##### `crossrepo config global init` {#crossrepo-config-global-init}

```console
crossrepo config global init [OPTIONS]
```

Write the config file that applies everywhere, unless it is already there.

##### `crossrepo config global reset` {#crossrepo-config-global-reset}

```console
crossrepo config global reset [OPTIONS] KEY
```

Take KEY out of the config file that applies everywhere, so its default applies.

Takes `KEY`.

##### `crossrepo config global set` {#crossrepo-config-global-set}

```console
crossrepo config global set [OPTIONS] KEY VALUES...
```

Set KEY to VALUES in the config file that applies everywhere.

Takes `KEY` and `VALUES...`.

##### `crossrepo config global show` {#crossrepo-config-global-show}

```console
crossrepo config global show [OPTIONS]
```

Print the config file that applies everywhere.

### `crossrepo get` {#crossrepo-get}

```console
crossrepo get [OPTIONS] SPEC
```

Fetch \[owner/\]repo:path\[@version\] into the cache and print its path.

The path is the only thing written to standard output, so the command
composes in a shell pipeline. When no version is given, the one chosen is
named on standard error; when one is given and the file has changed since,
that is said there instead.

Takes `SPEC`.

| Option | |
|---|---|
| `-o, --out PATH` | also write a copy here |
| `-u, --url` | print the URL of the version instead of downloading it |
| `--config PATH` | path to config.toml |
| `--refresh` | rescan repos instead of using the cached catalog |

### `crossrepo info` {#crossrepo-info}

```console
crossrepo info [OPTIONS] SPEC
```

Print everything the catalog holds about \[owner/\]repo:path\[@version\].

Addressed exactly as `crossrepo get` addresses it, so asking about a file
and fetching it differ in the verb and nothing else. Nothing is downloaded.
The same lines `crossrepo.info` prints in a notebook.

Takes `SPEC`.

| Option | |
|---|---|
| `--config PATH` | path to config.toml |
| `--refresh` | rescan repos instead of using the cached catalog |

### `crossrepo list` {#crossrepo-list}

```console
crossrepo list [OPTIONS] [REPO]
```

List result files, optionally limited to one repo.

Four columns: which repository, which file, where reading it goes, and what
it holds. They are what a file is chosen on, and they are the same four
`crossrepo.list` shows in a notebook, so that a listing is one thing however
it is read. Everything known about one file is `crossrepo info`.

Takes `[REPO]`.

| Option | |
|---|---|
| `-p, --pattern GLOB` | filter by filename glob, e.g. '*.csv' |
| `--json` | print machine readable output |
| `--config PATH` | path to config.toml |
| `--refresh` | rescan repos instead of using the cached catalog |

### `crossrepo refresh` {#crossrepo-refresh}

```console
crossrepo refresh [OPTIONS]
```

Rescan the repos and store the catalog.

A progress bar is drawn, one step per repository, when standard error is a
terminal. Any root, organisation or repository that could not be read is
named on standard error afterwards; the catalog is still written from what
could be, and the status stays zero, since a scan that reached most of its
sources has done its job.

| Option | |
|---|---|
| `--config PATH` | path to config.toml |
| `--refresh` | rescan repos instead of using the cached catalog |

### `crossrepo repos` {#crossrepo-repos}

```console
crossrepo repos [OPTIONS]
```

Print one line per repo holding result files.

| Option | |
|---|---|
| `--config PATH` | path to config.toml |
| `--refresh` | rescan repos instead of using the cached catalog |

### `crossrepo share` {#crossrepo-share}

```console
crossrepo share [OPTIONS] PATH DESCRIPTION
```

Publish PATH, saying in DESCRIPTION what it holds.

Publishing is naming a file in the crossrepo.yml, and this is that written
for you: the file is checked, the manifest is updated, and a file published
as a symbolic link is stamped as well. Committing the crossrepo.yml is what
makes the new version.

PATH has to be tracked by git already, since committing a file is the act of
offering it. A symbolic link is published instead of its content, so what it
points at must *not* be tracked: a target git holds as well would be
published twice, once as bytes and once as a stamp that could disagree.

Takes `PATH` and `DESCRIPTION`.

| Option | |
|---|---|
| `--config PATH` | path to config.toml |
| `--refresh` | rescan repos instead of using the cached catalog |

### `crossrepo stamp` {#crossrepo-stamp}

```console
crossrepo stamp [OPTIONS] [PATH]
```

Record what the published symbolic links in a repository point at.

A result file too large to commit is published as a symbolic link to
wherever the pipeline wrote it, together with a stamp in the ``crossrepo.yml``
saying which content the link stands for. Git versions the link and not the
bytes, so it is the stamp that makes the version: this command writes it,
and committing the manifest publishes the new version.

Only the two stamp lines of each entry are rewritten, so comments and
formatting survive and a stamping run reads as itself in a diff. A file must
already be named in the manifest to be stamped, naming it being how it is
published in the first place.

Takes `[PATH]`.

| Option | |
|---|---|
| `--check` | say what is out of date and write nothing; for a hook or for CI |

### `crossrepo versions` {#crossrepo-versions}

```console
crossrepo versions [OPTIONS] SPEC
```

Print the history of one result file, given as \[owner/\]repo:path.

Takes `SPEC`.

| Option | |
|---|---|
| `--config PATH` | path to config.toml |
| `--refresh` | rescan repos instead of using the cached catalog |
